The '''2020–21 Ekstraklasa''' (also known as '''PKO Bank Polski Ekstraklasa''' due to its [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] by [[PKO Bank Polski]])<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/pko-bank-polski-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy-13894 |title=PKO Bank Polski partnerem tytularnym Ekstraklasy |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=28 June 2019 |access-date=28 June 2019 |language=pl |archive-date=1 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701062604/http://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/pko-bank-polski-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy-13894 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvp.info/43235057/pko-bp-sponsorem-tytularnym-pilkarskiej-ekstraklasy |title=PKO BP sponsorem tytularnym piłkarskiej Ekstraklasy |publisher=tvp.info |date=26 June 2019 |access-date=26 June 2019 |language=pl}}</ref> was the 95th season of [[List of Polish football champions|the Polish Football Championship]], the 87th season of [[Sports league|the highest tier domestic division]] in the [[Polish football league system]] since its establishment in [[1927 Ekstraklasa|1927]] and the 13th season of the [[Ekstraklasa]] under its current title. The league was operated by the Ekstraklasa [[S.A. (corporation)|SA]].

The regular season was played as a [[round-robin tournament]]. A total of 16 teams participated, 13 of which competed in the league during the [[2019–20 Ekstraklasa|previous season]], while the remaining three were promoted from the [[2019–20 I liga]]. On 24 July 2020 Ekstraklasa SA and [[Polish Football Association]] announced the 2020–21 season calendar. The season started on 21 August 2020 and concluded on 16 May 2021. Due to the season start being delayed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland|COVID-19 pandemic]] it was shortened to 30 matchdays without a split into Championship and Relegation groups. Each team played a total of 30 matches, half at home and half away. After the 14th matchday the league went on a winter break between 21 December 2020 and 28 January 2021. 2020–21 was a transition season (only the team which took 16th position after the season was relegated to [[I liga]]) to extend Ekstraklasa from 16 to 18 teams starting with the [[2021–22 Ekstraklasa|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pzpn.pl/public/system/files/site_content/635/3379-40.KOMUNIKAT%20ZARZ%C4%84DU%2021.02.2020.pdf |title=KOMUNIKAT ZARZĄDU PZPN II/2020 Z DNIA 21 LUTEGO 2020 ROKU |publisher=pzpn.pl |date=21 February 2020 |access-date=20 July 2020}}</ref> During 2020–21 season a substitution limit increased from three to five.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/zmiany-w-regulaminie-rozgrywek-ekstraklasy-i-kalendarz-nowego-sezonu-14847 |title=Zmiany w regulaminie rozgrywek Ekstraklasy i kalendarz nowego sezonu |publisher=Ekstraklasa |date=24 July 2020 |access-date=25 July 2020 |archive-date=25 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725202026/https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/zmiany-w-regulaminie-rozgrywek-ekstraklasy-i-kalendarz-nowego-sezonu-14847 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was the fourth Ekstraklasa season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]]. Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], only 51 matches were played with a limited number of spectators. The rest of the matches (between 17 October 2020 and 15 May 2021) were played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] without any spectators.

The two clubs promoted from [[2019–20 I liga|I liga]] were [[Podbeskidzie Bielsko-Biała]], returning to Ekstraklasa after four years,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/gorale-na-szczycie-podbeskidzie-wraca-do-ekstraklasy-14806 |title=Górale na szczycie! Podbeskidzie wraca do Ekstraklasy |publisher=Ekstraklasa |date=15 July 2020 |access-date=20 July 2020 |archive-date=20 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720224124/https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/gorale-na-szczycie-podbeskidzie-wraca-do-ekstraklasy-14806 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as well as [[Stal Mielec]], who made a return to Ekstraklasa after 24 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/24-lata-czekania-stal-mielec-znow-w-ekstraklasie-14819 |title=24 lata czekania. Stal Mielec znów w Ekstraklasie! |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=17 July 2020 |access-date=20 July 2020 |archive-date=20 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720233648/https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/24-lata-czekania-stal-mielec-znow-w-ekstraklasie-14819 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After winning the [[2019–20 I liga#Promotion play-offs|I liga promotion play-offs]], [[Warta Poznań]] also returned to Ekstraklasa after 25 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/wygrali-baraze-warta-poznan-ponownie-w-ekstraklasie-14858 |title=Wygrali baraże! Warta Poznań ponownie w Ekstraklasie! |publisher=ekstraklasa.org |date=31 July 2020 |access-date=1 August 2020 |archive-date=9 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809121328/http://ekstraklasa.org/aktualnosci/wygrali-baraze-warta-poznan-ponownie-w-ekstraklasie-14858 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Legia Warsaw]] were the defending champions, and won their 15th title overall on 28 April after [[Raków Częstochowa]] drew 0–0 away to [[Jagiellonia Białystok]] with three games remaining.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/311/news3115531-Legia-mistrzem-Polski.html |title=Legia mistrzem Polski |publisher=90minut.pl |date=28 April 2021 |access-date=28 April 2021}}</ref> The season's runner-up was [[Raków Częstochowa]], and the third-placed team was [[Pogoń Szczecin]]. The only relegated team this season was [[Podbeskidzie Bielsko-Biała]].

==Teams==
A total of 16 teams participate in the 2020–21 Ekstraklasa season.
